claim.claim-text: The armor system (2400) of claim 68, wherein the viscoelastic memory-foam layer (2408) attenuates hypervelocity ballistic impacts exceeding 180 g down to <14.5 g at the cooling liner (2412) while recovering at least 96% of incident kinetic energy as combined piezoelectric pulses and harvestable thermal enthalpy.

The armor system (2400) of claim 68, wherein the dielectric Bragg mirror (2402) reflects at least 92% of incident 1,064 nm laser radiation while the 4H-SiC thermophotovoltaic and Bi2Te3 stratum (2406) generates between +640 We and +1,850 We of surge electrical power during sustained directed-energy irradiation.

An atmospheric-condensing tri-mode return-fire system (2500) powered by the supercapacitor bank (2420) and a -78 deg C cryogenic bus (2422) of the armor system (2400) of claim 68, comprising: (a) a centrifugal cyclone intake (2504) configured to draw ambient atmospheric gases and suspended particulates (2506) into a -78 deg C cryogenic condensation mold (2508); (b) a 33.6 kV ZVS plasma sintering electrode (2510) configured to fuse condensed atmospheric gases and particulates within the mold (2508) into a solid composite projectile (2512); and (c) a multi-stage linear induction coilgun barrel (2516) energized by the supercapacitor bank (2420) to accelerate the solid composite projectile (2512) to hypervelocity without chemical propellants.

The return-fire system (2500) of claim 71, further comprising a rotary breech selector (2518) that selectively diverts supercapacitor power and condensed atmospheric gas to a 0.55 T Sm2Co17 Halbach magnetic nozzle (2520) to launch 4,800 K toroidal plasma bolts at 1,850 m/s.

The return-fire system (2500) of claim 71, wherein the rotary breech selector (2518) selectively energizes a cryogenically cooled 1,064 nm Yb:YAG laser resonator (2522) to emit 10 Hz pulsed directed-energy return fire through a sapphire aperture (2524).
